acceptance.item: Definition: the process is an ordinary editable, versioned definition in the platform tenant
acceptance.today: SHIPPED (G9): the definition platform.register_tenant v1 is seeded into the platform tenant as an ordinary, unstamped, editable definition (mix letflow.seed.platform_definitions; since T-2739 also seeded automatically at boot when LETFLOW_SEED_PLATFORM_DEFINITIONS=true and by the QA deploy, which runs a smoke check that fails the deploy when it is missing; the document is lib/letflow/platform_processes/definition.ex, the seed lib/letflow/platform_processes/seed.ex). The seed never replaces a newer version an administrator made. The seed signs the switch-on with a REAL platform administrator: LETFLOW_PLATFORM_ACTIVATOR_USER_ID names that administrator (a user id of the platform tenant) and is OPTIONAL -- without it the first PLATFORM_ADMIN holder of the platform tenant signs (sorted by id, so the choice is the same on every run); a platform tenant with no such administrator is answered no_platform_activator and nothing is written. The process is still ROUTE CODE: the engine does not run the definition's platform steps yet and the routes still call the functions directly
acceptance.target: definition platform.register_tenant exists in the platform tenant, not module-stamped, v1 active after the seed, every edit a new draft
acceptance.proof: the seed's own tests: test/letflow/platform_processes/seed_test.exs (created and switched on, idempotent, a newer administrator version is kept, the version is editable); the document's tests: test/letflow/platform_processes/definition_test.exs; runner step A1 of BP-PLATFORM-01-register-tenant reads the active platform.register_tenant definition and saves its id; source: lib/letflow/routers/definitions.ex

title: Check a certificate by its public handle (no login)
description: Anyone holding the one-time public handle of an issued certificate (printed or sent by the exam application, BP-EXAM) opens the public page /verify/<handle> without signing in and sees whether the certificate is valid. The page lives in the core web router outside the login; the exam application only issues the handle.

actors.permission: none: public read, rate limited per address

preconditions: a certificate was issued and its public handle was given out (BP-EXAM, task 'get the certificate')

tasks.result: the page reads the public API with the handle from the address and shows the certificate data, or a not-found notice
200 with the public projection of the certificate; an unknown kind or unknown handle gets the same 404; responses carry no-store, no-referrer and noindex headers

outputs: the public view of the certificate
refusals: unknown or wrong handle: 404, identical to an unknown kind
too many lookups from one address: rate limited by the PublicReadRateLimit plug
uat: planned: a runner scenario needs an issued certificate (BP-EXAM) and a public GET step without a token
gap: no runner scenario yet; web page covered only by component tests if any
